title.zh: 卷18 列傳第10 王羆 王思政
title.en: Volume 18 Biographies 10: Wang Pi; Wang Sizheng
title.raw: 卷18 列傳第10 王羆 王思政 Volume 18 Biographies 10: Wang Pi; Wang Sizheng

sentences.zh: 王羆 子慶遠 孫述 王思政

translations.literal: Wang Pi; his son Qingyuan; his grandson Shu; Wang Sizheng
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi — Qingyuan — Shu — Wang Sizheng

sentences.zh: 王羆字熊羆，京兆霸城人，漢河南尹王遵之後，世為州郡著姓。

translations.literal: Wang Pi, styled Xiongpi, was a native of Bachecheng in Jingzhao commandery, a descendant of Wang Zun, governor of Henan under Han, for generations a prominent surname in the provinces and commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi, styled Xiongpi, came from Bachecheng in Jingzhao commandery. He descended from Wang Zun, governor of Henan under the Han, and his family had long been a leading name in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 羆剛直木強，處物平當，州郡敬憚之。

translations.literal: Pi was upright, stubborn, and unyielding; in dealing with things he was fair and even; the provinces and commanderies respected and feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi was blunt, stubborn, and scrupulously fair, and officials across the provinces both admired and feared him.

sentences.zh: 魏太和中，除殿中將軍。

translations.literal: In Wei Emperor Xiaowen's Taihe era, he was appointed palace-guard general.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taihe era of Emperor Xiaowen of Wei he was made palace-guard general.

sentences.zh: 先是南岐、東益氐羌反叛，王師戰不利，乃令羆領羽林五千鎮梁州，討平諸賊。

translations.literal: Previously Southern Qi and East Yizhou Di and Qiang had rebelled; the imperial army fought unfavorably; he was then ordered to lead five thousand Yulin guards to garrison Liang Province and pacify the various rebels.
translations.idiomatic: When Di and Qiang rebels rose in Southern Qi and East Yizhou and the imperial army faltered, Wang Pi was sent with five thousand Yulin guards to garrison Liang Province and put down the uprisings.

sentences.zh: 還，授右將軍、西河內史。

translations.literal: Returning, he was granted right general and interior minister of West He.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was given the posts of right general and interior minister of West He commandery.

sentences.zh: 辭不拜。

translations.literal: He declined and did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 時人謂之曰：「西河大邦，俸祿殷厚，何為致辭？

translations.literal: People of the time said to him: "West He is a great commandery; stipend and salary are abundant—why make yourself decline?"
translations.idiomatic: People asked him: "West He is a rich commandery with a generous salary. Why turn it down?"

sentences.zh: 」羆曰：「京洛材木，盡出西河，朝貴營第宅者，皆有求假。

translations.literal: Pi said: "Timber for the capital at Luoyang all comes from West He; court nobles building mansions all have requests to borrow.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi answered: "All the timber for Luoyang comes from West He, and every court noble building a mansion comes asking to borrow it.

sentences.zh: 如其私辦，卽力所不堪，若科發民間，又違法憲。

translations.literal: If by my own means I supply it, I immediately cannot bear the burden; if I levy it from the common people, I again violate law and charter.
translations.idiomatic: If I pay for it myself, I cannot afford it; if I levy it from the people, I break the law.

sentences.zh: 以此辭耳。」

translations.literal: For this reason I decline—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: That is why I declined."

sentences.zh: 梁將曹義宗圍荊州，勑羆與別將裴衍率兵赴救。

translations.literal: Liang general Cao Yizong besieged Jing Province; an edict ordered Pi together with separate commander Pei Yan to lead troops to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang general Cao Yizong besieged Jing Province, an edict sent Wang Pi with separate commander Pei Yan to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 遂與梁人戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Thereupon they fought the Liang men and greatly defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: They met the Liang army and routed it.

sentences.zh: 于時諸方鼎沸，所在凋殘。

translations.literal: At that time all quarters boiled like a cauldron; everywhere was wasted and ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The realm was in turmoil and every region lay in ruins.

sentences.zh: 荊州新經寇難，尤藉慰撫。

translations.literal: Jing Province had newly suffered raids and turmoil and especially needed comfort and soothing.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Province had just endured invasion and desperately needed reassurance and repair.

sentences.zh: 以羆為荊州刺史，進號撫軍將軍。

translations.literal: Pi was made governor of Jing Province; his title was advanced to general who pacifies the army.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi was appointed governor of Jing Province and promoted to general who pacifies the army.

sentences.zh: 梁復遣曹義宗衆數萬圍荊州，堰水灌城，不沒者數板。

translations.literal: Liang again sent Cao Yizong with a host of tens of thousands to besiege Jing Province; they dammed the water to flood the city, and only several boards of wall remained unsubmerged.
translations.idiomatic: Liang sent Cao Yizong back with tens of thousands of men, dammed the river, and flooded the city until only a few courses of wall stood above the water.

sentences.zh: 時旣內外多虞，未遑救援，乃遺羆鐵券，云城全當授本州刺史。

translations.literal: At that time both within and without there were many worries; there was no leisure to send relief; they therefore sent Pi an iron certificate, saying if the city remained whole he would be granted governor of that province.
translations.idiomatic: With crises on every front the court could spare no relief force, but it sent Wang Pi an iron certificate promising him the governorship if he kept the city intact.

sentences.zh: 城中糧盡，羆煮粥，與將士均分而食之。

translations.literal: Inside the city grain was exhausted; Pi cooked gruel and divided it equally with officers and soldiers to eat.
translations.idiomatic: When food ran out inside the walls, Wang Pi cooked gruel and shared it equally with his officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 每出戰，嘗不擐甲冑，大呼曰：「荊州城，孝文皇帝所置。

translations.literal: Each time he went out to battle he usually did not don armor; he shouted loudly: "Jing Province city was established by Emperor Xiaowen.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he fought he often went without armor and cried out: "This city of Jing Province was founded by Emperor Xiaowen.

sentences.zh: 天若不佑國家，使賊箭中王羆；

translations.literal: If Heaven does not protect the state, let the rebels' arrows strike Wang Pi;
translations.idiomatic: If Heaven will not save the realm, let the enemy's arrows find Wang Pi;

sentences.zh: 不爾，王羆須破賊。

translations.literal: If not, Wang Pi must break the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: If not, Wang Pi will break the enemy."

sentences.zh: 」屢經戰陣，亦不被傷。

translations.literal: He repeatedly passed through battle formations and was also not wounded.
translations.idiomatic: He fought again and again and was never hurt.

sentences.zh: 彌曆三年，義宗方退。

translations.literal: More than three years passed before Yizong finally withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Three years passed before Cao Yizong finally withdrew.

sentences.zh: 進封霸城縣公。

translations.literal: His rank was advanced to Duke of Bachecheng county.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Duke of Bachecheng.

sentences.zh: 尋遷車騎大將軍、涇州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to grand general of chariots and cavalry and governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made grand general of chariots and cavalry and governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 未及之部，屬太祖徵兵為勤王之舉，請前驅效命，遂為大都督，鎮華州。

translations.literal: Before he reached his post, it happened that the Grand Progenitor raised troops for the campaign to rescue the ruler; he requested to serve as vanguard and give his life; he thereupon became grand commander and garrisoned Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took office, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai mobilized for the rescue of the emperor; Wang Pi volunteered for the vanguard, was made grand commander, and garrisoned Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武西遷，拜驃騎大將軍，加侍中、開府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Pi was appointed grand general of fast cavalry, with additional posts as palace attendant and opening-the-feudatory.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu fled west, Wang Pi received the rank of grand general of fast cavalry, with palace attendant and opening-the-feudatory as well.

sentences.zh: 嘗修州城未畢，梯在外。

translations.literal: Once when repairing the provincial city walls was not yet complete, the ladders were outside.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while the provincial walls were still under repair, the siege ladders stood outside the unfinished works.

sentences.zh: 齊神武遣韓軌、司馬子如從河東宵濟襲羆，羆不之覺。

translations.literal: Gao Huan sent Han Gui and Sima Ziru to cross the Yellow River by night from Hedong and raid Pi; Pi did not notice.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan sent Han Gui and Sima Ziru to cross the Yellow River from Hedong by night and strike Wang Pi, who did not detect them.

sentences.zh: 比曉，軌衆已乘梯入城。

translations.literal: By dawn, Gui's troops had already mounted the ladders and entered the city.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn Han Gui's men were already climbing the ladders into the city.

sentences.zh: 羆尚臥未起，聞合外洶洶有聲，便袒身露髻徒跣，持一白挺，大呼而出。

translations.literal: Pi was still lying down and had not risen; hearing a clamorous noise outside the inner gate, he bared his torso, loosened his hair, went barefoot, grasped a white club, and shouted as he came out.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi was still in bed when he heard uproar at the gate. He threw off his clothes, let down his hair, went barefoot, seized a white club, and charged out shouting.

sentences.zh: 敵見之驚，逐至東門，左右稍集，合戰破之。

translations.literal: The enemy seeing him were startled; he drove them to the east gate; his attendants gradually gathered; they joined battle and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy fell back in shock. He drove them to the east gate, his men rallied around him, and together they broke the attack.

sentences.zh: 軌衆遂投城遁走。

translations.literal: Gui's troops thereupon leapt from the walls and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Han Gui's force then jumped from the walls and fled.

sentences.zh: 時關中大饑，徵稅民間穀食，以供軍費。

translations.literal: At that time Guanzhong suffered great famine; grain was levied from among the people to supply military expenses.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong was in famine, and grain was requisitioned from the people to feed the army.

sentences.zh: 或隱匿者，令遞相告，多被篣棰，以是人有逃散。

translations.literal: Those who concealed grain were ordered to inform on one another; many were beaten with bamboo rods, and thereby people fled and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone hiding grain was to be reported by his neighbors; many were flogged with bamboo, and people fled in fear.

sentences.zh: 唯羆信著于人，莫有隱者，得粟不少諸州，而無怨讟。

translations.literal: Only Pi's trustworthiness was renowned among the people; there were none who concealed; the grain obtained was not less than other provinces, yet without complaints and slander.
translations.idiomatic: Only in Wang Pi's jurisdiction did people trust him enough to surrender their grain willingly. He collected no less than other provinces, and no one complained.

sentences.zh: 沙苑之役，齊神武士馬甚盛。

translations.literal: At the Battle of Shaye, Gao Huan's troops and horses were very strong.
translations.idiomatic: At the Battle of Shaye, Gao Huan's army was overwhelming.

sentences.zh: 太祖以華州沖要，遣使勞羆，令加守備。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor because Huazhou was strategically critical sent an envoy to encourage Pi and ordered him to increase defensive preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Because Huazhou was a vital point, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai sent an envoy to encourage Wang Pi and told him to strengthen the defenses.

sentences.zh: 羆語使人曰：「老羆當道臥，貆子安得過！

translations.literal: Pi told the envoy: "Old Pi lies across the road—how can a badger cub get past!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi told the messenger: "Old Pi lies across the road. What badger cub thinks he can slip by?"

sentences.zh: 」太祖聞而壯之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor hearing it admired his spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai admired his boldness when he heard this.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武至城下，謂羆曰：「何不早降？

translations.literal: When Gao Huan reached beneath the walls, he said to Pi: "Why not surrender early?"
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan came beneath the walls he called to Wang Pi: "Why not surrender now?"

sentences.zh: 」羆乃大呼曰：「此城是王羆冢，生死在此，欲死者來。

translations.literal: Pi thereupon shouted loudly: "This city is Wang Pi's tomb; life and death are here—whoever wishes to die, come."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi shouted back: "This city is Wang Pi's tomb. Life and death are here. Whoever wants to die, come!"

sentences.zh: 」齊神武遂不敢攻。

translations.literal: Gao Huan thereupon did not dare attack.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan did not dare press the assault.

sentences.zh: 時茹茹渡河南寇，候騎已至豳州。

translations.literal: At that time the Rouran crossed south of the Yellow River to raid; scout cavalry had already reached Bin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: About then the Rouran crossed the Yellow River to raid, and their scouts had already reached Bin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 朝廷慮其深入，乃徵發士馬，屯守京城，塹諸街巷，以備侵軼。

translations.literal: The court feared they would penetrate deeply; troops and horses were levied to garrison the capital, ditches dug in all streets and lanes, to guard against incursions.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing a deep penetration, the court mobilized troops to hold the capital, dug trenches in every street, and braced for attack.

sentences.zh: 左僕射周惠達召羆議之。

translations.literal: Left vice director Zhou Huida summoned Pi to discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: Left vice director Zhou Huida summoned Wang Pi to consult him.

sentences.zh: 羆不應命，謂其使曰：「若茹茹至渭北者，王羆率鄉里自破之，不煩國家兵馬。

translations.literal: Pi did not respond to the summons; he told the envoy: "If the Rouran reach north of the Wei River, Wang Pi will lead the village folk to break them himself—no need to trouble the state's troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi ignored the summons and told the messenger: "If the Rouran reach the north bank of the Wei, Wang Pi will rally the local people and break them himself. There is no need to trouble the imperial army.

sentences.zh: 何為天子城中，遂作如此驚動。

translations.literal: Why in the Son of Heaven's city make such alarm and commotion?
translations.idiomatic: Why turn the Son of Heaven's own city into such a panic?

sentences.zh: 由周家小兒恇怯致此。

translations.literal: It is because the Zhou family's young fellow is cowardly that this has come about."
translations.idiomatic: This uproar comes from that coward Zhou boy."

sentences.zh: 」羆輕侮權勢，守正不回，皆此類也。

translations.literal: Pi slighted authority and power, held to the upright and did not bend—all were of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi scorned power, held to principle, and never bent—this was typical of him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，還鎮河東。

translations.literal: Before long, he returned to garrison Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he returned to garrison Hedong.

sentences.zh: 羆性儉率，不事邊幅。

translations.literal: Pi by nature was frugal and plain; he did not attend to niceties of appearance.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi was plain and frugal by nature and cared nothing for appearances.

sentences.zh: 嘗有臺使，羆為其設食。

translations.literal: Once there was an imperial envoy; Pi set out food for him.
translations.idiomatic: Once when an imperial envoy came, Wang Pi served him a meal.

sentences.zh: 使乃裂其薄餅緣。

translations.literal: The envoy then tore off the rim of his thin cake.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy tore away the crust of his flatbread.

sentences.zh: 羆曰：「耕種收穫，其功已深；

translations.literal: Pi said: "In plowing and sowing, harvesting—the labor is already deep;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pi said: "From plowing and sowing through the harvest, the labor is long;

sentences.zh: 舂爨造成，用力不少。

translations.literal: Pounding and cooking to make it—the effort is not small.
translations.idiomatic: and from threshing and cooking to the finished cake, the work is great.

sentences.zh: 乃爾選擇，當是未饑。

translations.literal: Yet you choose like this—you cannot yet be hungry."
translations.idiomatic: If you can pick and choose like that, you cannot be hungry yet."

sentences.zh: 」命左右撤去之。

translations.literal: He ordered his attendants to remove it.
translations.idiomatic: He had his attendants take the food away.

sentences.zh: 使者愕然大慙。

translations.literal: The envoy was startled and greatly ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy was stunned and deeply ashamed.

sentences.zh: 又有客與羆食瓜，〔客削瓜〕侵膚稍厚，羆意嫌之。

translations.literal: There was also a guest dining with Pi on melon; (Ke xiao gua) [emended: the guest pared the melon], cutting the flesh rather thick; Pi inwardly disliked it.
translations.idiomatic: Another time a guest shared melon with Wang Pi and cut away rather too much flesh, which Wang Pi quietly resented.

sentences.zh: 及瓜皮落地，乃引手就地，取而食之。

translations.literal: When the melon rind fell to the ground, he reached his hand to the ground, picked it up, and ate it.
translations.idiomatic: When the rind fell to the floor, he reached down, picked it up, and ate it.

sentences.zh: 客甚有愧色。

translations.literal: The guest was deeply ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: The guest flushed with shame.

sentences.zh: 性又嚴急，嘗有吏挾私陳事者，羆不暇命捶扑，乃手自取鞾履，持以擊之。

translations.literal: His nature was also strict and sharp; once when a clerk brought a private matter for judgment, Pi had no leisure to order flogging; he himself took off boot and shoe and struck him with them.
translations.idiomatic: He was harsh as well. Once when a clerk came with a private petition, Wang Pi did not bother to order a beating; he pulled off his boot and struck the man with it.

sentences.zh: 每至享會，親自秤量酒肉，分給將士。

translations.literal: Each time there was a feast, he personally weighed wine and meat and distributed it to officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: At every feast he personally weighed out wine and meat and divided it among the officers and soldiers.

sentences.zh: 時人尚其均平，嗤其鄙碎。

translations.literal: People of the time admired his evenhandedness and mocked his petty minuteness.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries respected his fairness but laughed at his fussiness.

sentences.zh: 大統七年，卒於鎮，贈太尉。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Datong, he died at his garrison post; posthumously given grand commandant.
translations.idiomatic: In Datong 7 (541) he died at his post and was posthumously made grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 子慶遠，弱冠以功臣子拜直閤將軍。

translations.literal: His son Qingyuan, at weak-crown age as a meritorious minister's son was appointed direct-pavilion general.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qingyuan, still in his teens and as the son of a meritorious minister, was made direct-pavilion general.

sentences.zh: 先羆卒，孫述嗣。

translations.literal: Qingyuan died before Pi; his grandson Shu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Qingyuan died before Wang Pi, and the grandson Shu inherited the line.

sentences.zh: 述字長述，少聰敏，有識度。

translations.literal: Shu, styled Changshu, from youth was quick and clever, with knowledge and measure.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, styled Changshu, was clever from boyhood and showed unusual judgment.

sentences.zh: 年八歲，太祖見而奇之，曰：「王公有此孫，足為不朽。

translations.literal: At age eight, the Grand Progenitor saw him and thought him remarkable, saying: "Duke Wang has this grandson—enough to be immortal."
translations.idiomatic: When he was eight, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai met him, was impressed, and said: "Duke Wang has a grandson like this; his name will endure."

sentences.zh: 」卽以為鎮遠將軍，拜太子舍人。

translations.literal: He was immediately made general who pacifies the distant and appointed attendant to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was at once made general who pacifies the distant and attendant to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 以祖憂去職。

translations.literal: Because of mourning for his grandfather he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He left office to mourn his grandfather.

sentences.zh: 述幼喪父，為羆所鞠養。

translations.literal: Shu from youth lost his father; he was reared and nurtured by Pi.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had lost his father young and was raised by Wang Pi.

sentences.zh: 及居喪，深合禮度。

translations.literal: When he observed mourning, he deeply conformed to ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: In mourning he observed every requirement of ritual with deep sincerity.

sentences.zh: 于時東西交爭，金革方始，羣官遭喪者，卒哭之後，皆起令視事。

translations.literal: At that time east and west were at war; weapons and armor had just begun; officials who encountered mourning, after the end-of-mourning wailing, all were made to rise and handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: War had just broken out between east and west, and officials in mourning were normally ordered back to duty after the final wailing rites.

sentences.zh: 述請終禮制，辭理懇切。

translations.literal: Shu requested to complete the full mourning regulations; his words and reasoning were earnest.
translations.idiomatic: Shu asked to finish the full mourning period instead, pleading his case with earnest force.

sentences.zh: 太祖令中使就視，知其哀毀，乃特許之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor ordered a palace envoy to go observe; knowing his grief and emaciation, he specially permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai sent a palace envoy to see him, and when he saw how deeply Shu was grieving and wasting away, he granted an exception.

sentences.zh: 喪畢，襲爵扶風郡公，累遷上大將軍。

translations.literal: When mourning was complete, he inherited the title Duke of Fufeng commandery; by successive promotion he reached supreme general.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he inherited the dukedom of Fufeng and rose by stages to supreme general.

sentences.zh: 王思政字思政，太原祁人。

translations.literal: Wang Sizheng, styled Sizheng, was a native of Qi in Taiyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng, styled Sizheng, came from Qi in Taiyuan commandery.

sentences.zh: 容貌魁偉，有籌策。

translations.literal: His appearance was tall and imposing; he had stratagems and plans.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall and imposing, with a strategist's mind.

sentences.zh: 魏正光中，解褐員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: In Wei Emperor Xiaoming's Zhenguang era, he entered service as attendant gentleman of scattered cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguang era of Emperor Xiaoming of Wei he entered office as attendant gentleman of scattered cavalry.

sentences.zh: 屬万俟醜奴、宿勤明達等擾亂關右，北海王顥率兵討之，啟思政隨軍。

translations.literal: It happened that Wanqij Chounu, Suqin Mingda, and others disturbed Guan-you; Prince of Beihai, Yuan Hao, led troops to subdue them and memorialized that Sizheng follow the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Wanqij Chounu, Suqin Mingda, and others ravaged Guan-you, Prince Yuan Hao of Beihai marched against them and asked that Wang Sizheng accompany the campaign.

sentences.zh: 軍事所有謀議，竝與之參詳。

translations.literal: In all military affairs there were counsel and deliberation; he was jointly consulted with in the details.
translations.idiomatic: On every military question Hao consulted him in detail.

sentences.zh: 時魏孝武在藩，素聞其名，顥軍還，乃引為賓客，遇之甚厚。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Xiaowu of Wei was at his fief; he had long heard his name; when Hao's army returned, he drew him in as a guest and treated him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu, then still at his princely fief, had long known Wang Sizheng's reputation. When Hao returned, the prince took him on as a client and treated him with great favor.

sentences.zh: 及登大位，委以心膂，遷安東將軍。

translations.literal: When he ascended the great throne, he entrusted him as heart and spine, transferred to general who pacifies the east.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowu took the throne he made Wang Sizheng one of his closest confidants and promoted him to general who pacifies the east.

sentences.zh: 預定策功，封祁縣侯。

translations.literal: He shared in the merit of fixing the succession; was enfeoffed Marquis of Qi county.
translations.idiomatic: For his part in securing the succession he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Qi county.

sentences.zh: 俄而齊神武潛有異圖，帝以思政可任大事，拜中軍大將軍、大都督，總宿衛兵。

translations.literal: Soon Gao Huan secretly had a different design; the emperor because Sizheng could be entrusted with great affairs appointed him grand general of the central army, grand commander, overall commander of palace-guard troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan began plotting in secret, the emperor judged Wang Sizheng fit for the gravest duties and made him grand general of the central army, grand commander, and overall commander of the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 思政乃言於帝曰：「高歡之心，行路所共知矣。

translations.literal: Sizheng then spoke to the emperor, saying: "Gao Huan's heart—the road travelers all know it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng then told the emperor: "Everyone on the road knows what Gao Huan intends.

sentences.zh: 洛陽四面受敵，非用武之地。

translations.literal: Luoyang on four sides receives enemies—it is not a place for wielding weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang is beset on every side. It is no place to make a stand.

sentences.zh: 關中有崤、函之固，一人可禦萬夫。

translations.literal: Guanzhong has the fortifications of Xiao and Han; one man can oppose ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong has the passes of Xiao and Han, where one man can hold off ten thousand.

sentences.zh: 且士馬精強，糧儲委積，進可以討除逆命，退可以保據關、河。

translations.literal: Moreover troops and horses are keen and strong; grain stores piled up; advancing one can campaign to eliminate rebellious mandates; retreating one can hold and secure the passes and the river.
translations.idiomatic: Its soldiers and horses are strong, its granaries full. From there one can advance to crush rebellion or fall back and hold the passes and the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 宇文夏州糾合同盟，願立功效。

translations.literal: Yuwen of Xia Province has rallied covenant allies and wishes to establish merit and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Tai of Xia Province has gathered the allied lords and is ready to serve.

sentences.zh: 若聞車駕西幸，必當奔走奉迎。

translations.literal: If he hears the imperial carriage will move west, he will surely run to meet and welcome it.
translations.idiomatic: If he hears that Your Majesty is moving west, he will hurry to meet you.

sentences.zh: 藉天府之資，因已成之業，一二年間，習戰陣，勸耕桑，修舊京，何慮不克。

translations.literal: Relying on the resources of the heavenly repository, following the already established enterprise—in one or two years, training in battle arrays, encouraging farming and sericulture, repairing the old capital—what worry that it cannot be achieved?"
translations.idiomatic: With the wealth of the western stronghold and a foundation already laid, in a year or two you can drill the army, restore agriculture, rebuild the old capital—what could stop you?"

sentences.zh: 」帝深然之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply convinced.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武兵至河北，帝乃西遷。

translations.literal: When Gao Huan's army reached Hebei, the emperor thereupon moved west.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Huan's army reached Hebei, the emperor fled west.

sentences.zh: 進爵太原郡公。

translations.literal: His rank was advanced to Duke of Taiyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng was promoted to Duke of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 大統之後，思政雖被任委，自以非相府之舊，每不自安。

translations.literal: After Datong, although Sizheng was entrusted with duties, he himself because he was not of the chancellor's mansion's old cohort, each time was not at ease.
translations.idiomatic: After Datong, though Wang Sizheng held important posts, he never felt secure, knowing he was not one of Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's old followers from the chancellor's household.

sentences.zh: 太祖曾在同州，與羣公宴集，出錦罽及雜綾絹數段，命諸將樗蒱取之。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor once was at Tong Province, with the various lords feasting and gathering; he produced several lengths of brocade felts and assorted silks and satins, and ordered the generals to obtain them by casting lots with yarrow stalks and game pieces.
translations.idiomatic: Once at Tong Province, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai feasted with the great lords, laid out lengths of brocade felt and assorted silks, and told the generals to win them by casting lots at chubo.

sentences.zh: 物旣盡，太祖又解所服金帶，令諸人遍擲，曰：「先得盧者，卽與之。

translations.literal: When the goods were exhausted, the Grand Progenitor again removed the gold belt he was wearing, ordered everyone to throw in turn, and said: "Whoever first gets lu shall receive it.
translations.idiomatic: When the prizes were gone, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai took off his own gold belt, had everyone take turns casting, and said: "Whoever throws lu first gets it.

sentences.zh: 」羣公將遍，莫有得者。

translations.literal: " The assembled lords were nearly through; none obtained it.
translations.idiomatic: " The lords went through nearly everyone; no one won.

sentences.zh: 次至思政，乃斂容跪坐而自誓曰：「王思政羇旅歸朝，蒙宰相國士之遇，方願盡心效命，上報知己。

translations.literal: When it came to Sizheng's turn, he composed his bearing, knelt and sat, and swore to himself, saying: "Wang Sizheng, a wanderer who returned to court, received from the chancellor the treatment of a national warrior; I only wish to give my heart and serve to the utmost, repaying one who knew me.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sizheng's turn came, he composed himself, knelt, and swore aloud: "Wang Sizheng came back to court as a stranger and was treated by the chancellor as a man of the realm; I mean to give my all and repay that trust.

sentences.zh: 若此誠有實，令宰相賜知者，願擲卽為盧；

translations.literal: If this sincerity is real, let the chancellor who knows me grant it—may my cast be lu at once;
translations.idiomatic: If this is true, let the chancellor who knows me grant it—may I throw lu at once;

sentences.zh: 若內懷不盡，神靈亦當明之，使不作也，便當殺身以謝所奉。

translations.literal: if within I harbor anything less, the spirits too should make it clear and keep it from coming out; then I should kill myself to answer what I serve.
translations.idiomatic: if my heart is not wholly true, let the spirits show it and keep the throw from winning; then I will kill myself to answer for my faith.

sentences.zh: 」辭氣慷慨，一坐盡驚。

translations.literal: " His words and tone were impassioned; the whole assembly was startled.
translations.idiomatic: " His words rang with passion; everyone present was stunned.

sentences.zh: 卽拔所佩刀，橫於膝上，攬樗蒱，拊髀擲之。

translations.literal: He at once drew the knife at his belt, laid it across his knees, gathered the chupu, and slapping his thigh cast.
translations.idiomatic: He drew the knife at his belt, laid it across his knees, took up the chupu, and cast with a slap on his thigh.

sentences.zh: 比太祖止之，已擲為盧矣。

translations.literal: By the time the Grand Progenitor stopped him, he had already cast lu.
translations.idiomatic: Before Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai could stop him, he had already thrown lu.

sentences.zh: 徐乃拜而受。

translations.literal: Then slowly he bowed and received it.
translations.idiomatic: Then he bowed and accepted the belt.

sentences.zh: 自此之後，太祖期寄更深。

translations.literal: From this time onward, the Grand Progenitor's expectations and trust in him grew deeper.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai trusted him still more.

sentences.zh: 轉驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to general of swift cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general of swift cavalry.

sentences.zh: 令募精兵，從獨孤信取洛陽，仍共信鎮之。

translations.literal: He was ordered to recruit picked troops, follow Dugu Xin to take Luoyang, and still garrison it together with Xin.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to raise picked troops, follow Dugu Xin to take Luoyang, and remain to garrison it with him.

sentences.zh: 及河橋之戰，思政下馬，用長矟左右橫擊，一擊踣數人。

translations.literal: At the battle of Heqiao, Sizheng dismounted, used a long spear to strike left and right across, and with one blow felled several men.
translations.idiomatic: At Heqiao Wang Sizheng dismounted and swept left and right with a long spear, felling several men with each blow.

sentences.zh: 時陷

translations.literal: At the time, having fallen into
translations.idiomatic: At the time he had fallen into

translations.literal: (harm)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: harm]

sentences.zh: 〔陣〕旣深，從者死盡，思政被重創悶絕。

translations.literal: [formation] already deep; attendants were all dead, and Sizheng received grievous wounds and lost consciousness.
translations.idiomatic: the enemy formation was already deeply breached; his escort was wiped out and Wang Sizheng was badly wounded and fell unconscious.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，敵將收軍。

translations.literal: It happened to be dusk, and the enemy general withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk the enemy commander broke off and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 思政久經軍旅，每戰唯著破弊甲，敵人疑非將帥，故免。

translations.literal: Sizheng had long experience in the army; in every battle he wore only worn and tattered armor, so the enemy doubted he was a commander and therefore spared him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng had long been in the field and always fought in ragged armor, so the enemy took him for no commander and let him be.

sentences.zh: 有帳下督雷五安于戰處哭求思政，會其已蘇，遂相得。

translations.literal: A tent guard under his command, Lei Wu'an, wept and searched for Sizheng on the battlefield; it happened that he had already revived, and they found each other.
translations.idiomatic: His tent guard Lei Wu'an searched the field in tears for Wang Sizheng and found him already awake.

sentences.zh: 乃割衣裹創，扶思政上馬，夜久方得還。

translations.literal: Thereupon he cut cloth to bind the wounds, helped Sizheng mount a horse, and only after a long night did they get back.
translations.idiomatic: He tore cloth to bind the wounds, helped Wang Sizheng onto a horse, and only late at night did they get back.

sentences.zh: 仍鎮弘農。

translations.literal: He still garrisoned Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: He continued to garrison Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 思政以玉壁地在險要，請築城。

translations.literal: Sizheng, because Yubi lay in a strategic strongpoint, requested to build a city.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng saw that Yubi occupied a strategic position and asked to build a fortress there.

sentences.zh: 卽自營度，移鎮之。

translations.literal: He thereupon laid out the works himself and moved his garrison there.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out the works himself and moved his garrison there.

sentences.zh: 遷幷州刺史，仍鎮玉壁。

translations.literal: He was transferred to governor of Bing Province and still garrisoned Yubi.
translations.idiomatic: He was made governor of Bing Province and continued to hold Yubi.

sentences.zh: 八年，東魏來寇，思政守禦有備，敵人晝夜攻圍，卒不能克，乃收軍還。

translations.literal: In the eighth year Eastern Wei came to raid; Sizheng's defense was prepared, and the enemy attacked and besieged day and night but in the end could not take it, and so withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Eastern Wei attacked; Wang Sizheng was ready, and though the enemy besieged the city day and night they could not take it and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 以全城功，受驃騎大將軍。

translations.literal: For the merit of preserving the whole city, he received grand general of swift cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: For holding the city intact he was made grand general of swift cavalry.

sentences.zh: 復命思政鎮弘農。

translations.literal: He was again ordered to have Sizheng garrison Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng was again ordered to garrison Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 於是修城郭，起樓櫓，營田農，積芻秣，凡可以守禦者，皆具焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he repaired walls and moats, raised towers and watchlofts, opened fields for farming, and stored fodder and grain—everything that could serve defense was provided.
translations.idiomatic: He repaired walls and moats, raised towers and watchlofts, opened fields, and stored fodder and grain—everything needed for defense.

sentences.zh: 弘農之有備，自思政始也。

translations.literal: Hongnong's being prepared began with Sizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Hongnong's defenses began with Wang Sizheng.

sentences.zh: 十二年，加特進、荊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was given specially advanced rank and made governor of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was given specially advanced rank and made governor of Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 州境卑濕，城塹多壞。

translations.literal: The province's territory was low and damp, and walls and moats were often ruined.
translations.idiomatic: The province was low and damp, and its walls and moats were often in ruins.

sentences.zh: 思政方命都督藺小歡督工匠繕治之。

translations.literal: Sizheng was just then ordering area commander Lin Xiaohuan to supervise craftsmen in repairing them.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng had area commander Lin Xiaohuan supervise craftsmen in repairing them.

sentences.zh: 掘得黃金三十斤，夜中密送之。

translations.literal: They dug up thirty jin of gold and secretly sent it to him at night.
translations.idiomatic: The workmen dug up thirty jin of gold and sent it to him secretly at night.

sentences.zh: 至旦，思政召佐吏以金示之，曰「人臣不宜有私」，悉封金送上。

translations.literal: At dawn Sizheng summoned his staff and showed them the gold, saying "A minister should not have private possessions," and sealed all the gold and sent it up.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Wang Sizheng summoned his staff, showed them the gold, and said, "A minister should keep no private hoard," then sealed it all and sent it to the court.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉之，賜錢二十萬。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor praised this and granted two hundred thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai praised him and gave him two hundred thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 思政之去玉壁也，太祖命舉代己者，思政乃進所部都督韋孝寬。

translations.literal: When Sizheng left Yubi, the Grand Progenitor ordered that someone be recommended to replace him; Sizheng thereupon advanced his subordinate area commander Wei Xiaokuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sizheng left Yubi, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai asked who should replace him; Wang Sizheng recommended his subordinate Wei Xiaokuan.

sentences.zh: 其後東魏來寇，孝寬卒能全城。

translations.literal: Afterward Eastern Wei came to raid, and Xiaokuan in the end was able to preserve the whole city.
translations.idiomatic: Later Eastern Wei attacked, and Wei Xiaokuan held the whole city.

sentences.zh: 時論稱其知人。

translations.literal: Opinion at the time praised him for knowing men.
translations.idiomatic: Contemporaries praised him for knowing men.

sentences.zh: 十三年，侯景叛東魏，擁兵梁、鄭，為東魏所攻。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year Hou Jing rebelled against Eastern Wei, held troops in Liang and Zheng, and was attacked by Eastern Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year Hou Jing rebelled against Eastern Wei, held Liang and Zheng with his army, and came under attack from Eastern Wei.

sentences.zh: 景乃請援乞師。

translations.literal: Jing thereupon requested aid and begged for troops.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing then asked for help and begged for troops.

sentences.zh: 當時未卽應接。

translations.literal: At the time they did not at once respond and join him.
translations.idiomatic: The court did not respond at once.

sentences.zh: 思政以為若不因機進取，後悔無及。

translations.literal: Sizheng thought that if they did not seize the opportunity and advance, regret would come too late.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng argued that if they missed the moment there would be no recovering it.

sentences.zh: 卽率荊州步騎萬餘，從魯關向陽翟。

translations.literal: He at once led more than ten thousand Jing Province foot and horse, went from Lu Pass toward Yangzhai.
translations.idiomatic: He at once led more than ten thousand foot and horse from Jing Province through Lu Pass toward Yangzhai.

sentences.zh: 思政入守潁川。

translations.literal: Sizheng entered and held Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng entered and held Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 景引兵向豫州，外稱略地，乃密遣送款於梁。

translations.literal: Jing led troops toward Yu Province, outwardly claiming to seize territory, but secretly sent submission to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing marched toward Yu Province, claiming to seize ground, but secretly offered submission to Liang.

sentences.zh: 思政分佈諸軍，據景七州十二鎮。

translations.literal: Sizheng deployed the various armies and held seven of Jing's provinces and twelve garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng deployed his forces and seized seven provinces and twelve garrisons from Hou Jing.

sentences.zh: 太祖乃以所授景使持節、太傅、大將軍、兼中書令、河南大行臺、河南諸軍事，回授思政。

translations.literal: The Grand Progenitor thereupon took the titles granted Jing—commissioner bearing the staff, grand tutor, grand general, concurrent director of the Masters of Writing, Henan mobile headquarters, and commander of all Henan military affairs—and transferred them back to Sizheng.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai then took the titles granted Hou Jing—commissioner bearing the staff, grand tutor, grand general, concurrent director of the Masters of Writing, Henan mobile headquarters, and commander of all Henan military affairs—and offered them to Wang Sizheng instead.

sentences.zh: 思政竝讓不受。

translations.literal: Sizheng together declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng declined them all.

sentences.zh: 頻使敦喻，唯受河南諸軍事。

translations.literal: Envoys repeatedly urged and instructed him; he accepted only commander of all Henan military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated envoys pressed him; he accepted only commander of all Henan military affairs.

sentences.zh: 東魏太尉高嶽、行臺慕容紹宗、儀同劉豐生等，率步騎十萬來攻潁川。

translations.literal: Eastern Wei's grand commandant Gao Yue, field secretariat Murong Shaozong, acting three-division Liu Fengsheng, and others led a hundred thousand foot and horse to attack Yingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Wei's grand commandant Gao Yue, field secretariat Murong Shaozong, acting three-division Liu Fengsheng, and others led a hundred thousand foot and horse against Yingchuan.

sentences.zh: 城內臥鼓偃旗，若無人者。

translations.literal: Within the city drums were stilled and banners lowered, as if there were no one.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the city drums were stilled and banners lowered, as if it were empty.

sentences.zh: 嶽恃其衆，謂一戰可屠，乃四面鼓噪而上。

translations.literal: Yue relied on his numbers, thinking one battle could slaughter them, and so from four sides raised a clamor and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yue trusted his numbers, thought one assault would overrun the place, and charged in from all sides with a great uproar.

sentences.zh: 思政選城中驍勇，開門出突。

translations.literal: Sizheng selected the city's fierce and brave, opened the gates, and sallied out in a sudden attack.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng picked the city's best fighters, opened the gates, and struck out.

sentences.zh: 嶽衆不敢當，引軍亂退。

translations.literal: Yue's host did not dare withstand them and withdrew the army in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yue's men could not stand against them and broke in disorder.

sentences.zh: 嶽知不可卒攻，乃多修營壘。

translations.literal: Yue knew it could not be taken in a sudden attack and therefore built many camps and ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yue saw he could not take the city at a rush and built many camps and ramparts.

sentences.zh: 又隨地勢高處，築土山以臨城中。

translations.literal: Again, following high ground in the terrain, he built earthen hills to overlook the city.
translations.idiomatic: He also piled earthen hills on high ground to overlook the city.

sentences.zh: 飛梯火車，晝夜攻之。

translations.literal: Flying ladders and fire carts attacked day and night.
translations.idiomatic: Flying ladders and fire carts assaulted it day and night.

sentences.zh: 思政亦作火攢，因迅風便投之土山。

translations.literal: Sizheng also made fire bundles and, taking advantage of a swift wind, cast them onto the earthen hills.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng made fire bundles too and, when the wind rose, hurled them onto the earthen hills.

sentences.zh: 又以火箭射之，燒其攻具。

translations.literal: Again with fire arrows he shot them and burned their siege engines.
translations.idiomatic: He also shot fire arrows and burned their siege engines.

sentences.zh: 仍募勇士，縋而出戰。

translations.literal: Still he recruited brave men and, lowering ropes, went out to fight.
translations.idiomatic: He still recruited brave men to let themselves down by rope and sally out.

sentences.zh: 嶽衆披靡，其守土山人亦棄山而走。

translations.literal: Yue's host was routed, and those guarding the earthen hills also abandoned the hills and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yue's army was routed, and the men on the earthen hills abandoned them and fled.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄更益嶽兵，堰洧水以灌城。

translations.literal: Wenxiang of Qi further reinforced Yue's troops and dammed the Wei River to flood the city.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng, Wenxiang of Qi, sent more troops to Gao Yue and dammed the Wei River to flood the city.

sentences.zh: 城中水泉湧溢，不可防止。

translations.literal: Within the city springs and wells overflowed and could not be stopped or blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Springs and wells inside the city overflowed and could not be stopped.

sentences.zh: 懸釜而炊，糧力俱竭。

translations.literal: They hung cauldrons to cook; grain and strength were both exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: They cooked from pots hung overhead; food and strength were both spent.

sentences.zh: 慕容紹宗、劉豐生及其將慕容永珍共乘樓船以望城內，令善射者俯射城中。

translations.literal: Murong Shaozong, Liu Fengsheng, and their general Murong Yongzhen together rode tower ships to look into the city and ordered skilled archers to shoot down into it.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Shaozong, Liu Fengsheng, and their officer Murong Yongzhen rode tower ships to look into the city and had skilled archers shoot down from above.

sentences.zh: 俄而大風暴起，船乃飄至城下。

translations.literal: Before long a great windstorm arose, and the ships drifted to below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a great wind rose and the ships drifted below the walls.

sentences.zh: 城上人以長鉤牽船，弓弩亂髮。

translations.literal: Men atop the walls used long hooks to pull the ships and shot bows and crossbows in confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Men on the walls hooked the ships with long poles and rained bowshot and bolts on them.

sentences.zh: 紹宗窮急，投水而死。

translations.literal: Shaozong, in extremity, threw himself into the water and died.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Shaozong, in desperation, threw himself into the water and drowned.

sentences.zh: 豐生浮向土山，復中矢而斃。

translations.literal: Fengsheng floated toward the earthen hill and again was hit by an arrow and died.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fengsheng floated toward the earthen hill and was struck again by an arrow and killed.

sentences.zh: 生擒永珍。

translations.literal: Yongzhen was captured alive.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yongzhen was taken alive.

sentences.zh: 思政謂之曰：「僕之破亡，在於晷漏。

translations.literal: Sizheng said to him: "My ruin is a matter of hours.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng told him: "My fall is only hours away.

sentences.zh: 誠知殺卿無益，然人臣之節，守之以死。

translations.literal: I truly know that killing you would be of no benefit, yet a minister's integrity is kept even unto death.
translations.idiomatic: I know killing you does no good, yet a minister's duty is kept even unto death.

sentences.zh: 」乃流涕斬之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon, weeping, he beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: " Then, weeping, he beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 幷收紹宗等尸，以禮埋瘞。

translations.literal: He also gathered the corpses of Shaozong and the others and buried them with rites.
translations.idiomatic: He also gathered the bodies of Murong Shaozong and the others and buried them with ceremony.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄聞之，乃率步騎十一萬來攻。

translations.literal: Wenxiang of Qi heard of this and thereupon led a hundred and ten thousand foot and horse to attack.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng heard of this and marched with a hundred and ten thousand foot and horse to attack.

sentences.zh: 自至堰下，督勵士卒。

translations.literal: He himself came to the dam and urged and encouraged the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He came in person to the dam and urged the troops on.

sentences.zh: 水壯，城北面遂崩。

translations.literal: The water swelled, and the north face of the city thereupon collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: The water rose, and the north wall of the city collapsed.

sentences.zh: 水便滿溢，無措足之地。

translations.literal: The water then overflowed everywhere, with no place to set a foot.
translations.idiomatic: Water flooded everywhere until there was nowhere to stand.

sentences.zh: 思政知事不濟，率左右據土山，謂之曰：「吾受國重任，本望平難立功。

translations.literal: Sizheng knew the affair would not succeed, led his close attendants to hold the earthen hill, and said to them: "I received the state's heavy charge and originally hoped to settle calamity and establish merit.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng saw all was lost, took his close attendants to the earthen hill, and told them: "I bore the state's heavy trust and meant to end this crisis and win merit.

sentences.zh: 精誠無感，遂辱王命。

translations.literal: Sincerity moved nothing; I have thus disgraced the royal command.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven did not answer my sincerity, and I have shamed the throne's charge.

sentences.zh: 今力屈道窮，計無所出。

translations.literal: Now strength is spent and the way is exhausted; no plan remains.
translations.idiomatic: Now my strength is spent and every road is closed; I have no plan left.

sentences.zh: 唯當效死，以謝朝恩。

translations.literal: I can only offer my death to answer the court's grace.
translations.idiomatic: I can only die to answer the court's grace.

sentences.zh: 」因仰天大哭。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he looked up to heaven and wept greatly.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he looked up to heaven and wept aloud.

sentences.zh: 左右皆號慟。

translations.literal: Those at his side all wailed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Those beside him all wailed.

sentences.zh: 思政西向再拜，便欲自刎。

translations.literal: Sizheng bowed twice facing west and was about to cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng bowed twice toward the west and was about to kill himself.

sentences.zh: 先是，齊文襄告城中人曰：「有能生致王大將軍者，封侯，重賞。

translations.literal: Earlier, Wenxiang of Qi had told the people in the city: "Whoever can bring in Grand General Wang alive shall be enfeoffed marquis and richly rewarded.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Gao Cheng had told the city: "Whoever brings in Grand General Wang alive will be made marquis and richly rewarded.

sentences.zh: 若大將軍身有損傷，親近左右，皆從大戮。

translations.literal: If Grand General Wang's person suffers injury, his close attendants and those near him shall all suffer great execution.
translations.idiomatic: If Grand General Wang is harmed, his close attendants will all be put to death.

sentences.zh: 」都督駱訓謂思政曰：「公常語訓等，但將我頭降，非但得富貴，亦是活一城人。

translations.literal: " Area commander Luo Xun said to Sizheng: "You often told Xun and the others, 'Just take my head and surrender—not only will you gain wealth and honor, you will also save a whole city of people.
translations.idiomatic: " Area commander Luo Xun said to Wang Sizheng: "You often told us, 'Take my head and surrender—you will win wealth and honor and save a whole city.

sentences.zh: 今高相旣有此言，公豈不哀城中士卒也！

translations.literal: Now the High Minister already has this word—will you not pity the soldiers in the city!
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng has already said as much—will you not pity the men in the city!

sentences.zh: 」固共止之，不得引決。

translations.literal: " They firmly together stopped him, and he could not carry out his resolve.
translations.idiomatic: " They held him back by force, and he could not kill himself.

sentences.zh: 齊文襄遣其常侍趙彥深就土山執手申意。

translations.literal: Wenxiang of Qi sent his regular attendant Zhao Yanshen to the earthen hill, took his hand, and conveyed his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng sent his regular attendant Zhao Yanshen to the earthen hill, took Wang Sizheng's hand, and spoke his mind.

sentences.zh: 引見文襄，辭氣慷慨，無撓屈之容。

translations.literal: He was led to an audience with Wenxiang; his words and tone were impassioned, with no appearance of bending or yielding.
translations.idiomatic: He was brought before Gao Cheng; his bearing was impassioned and unbroken.

sentences.zh: 文襄以其忠於所事，禮遇甚厚。

translations.literal: Wenxiang, because he was loyal to what he served, treated him with great courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng honored him greatly for his loyalty to his charge.

sentences.zh: 思政初入潁川，士卒八千人，城旣無外援，亦無叛者。

translations.literal: When Sizheng first entered Yingchuan he had eight thousand soldiers; though the city had no outside relief, there were also no deserters.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sizheng first entered Yingchuan he had eight thousand men; though no relief came from outside, not one deserted.

sentences.zh: 思政常以勤王為務，不營資產。

translations.literal: Sizheng always made saving the throne his task and did not build up assets.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng always made saving the throne his business and did not build up property.

sentences.zh: 嘗被賜園地，思政出征後，家人種桑果。

translations.literal: Once he had been granted an estate garden; after Sizheng went on campaign, his family planted mulberries and fruit.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had been granted an estate; after he marched out, his family planted mulberries and fruit trees.

sentences.zh: 及還，見而怒曰：「匈奴未滅，去病辭家，況大賊未平，何事產業！

translations.literal: When he returned and saw it, he angrily said: "The Xiongnu are not yet destroyed and Huo Qubing left home—how much more when the great enemy is not yet pacified, what business is there with estates!
translations.idiomatic: When he returned and saw it, he said in anger: "The Xiongnu were not yet destroyed when Huo Qubing left home—how much more now, with the great enemy still unbeaten, what business is there with estates!

sentences.zh: 」命左右拔而棄之。

translations.literal: " He ordered those at his side to pull them up and discard them.
translations.idiomatic: " He ordered his attendants to pull them up and throw them away.

sentences.zh: 故身陷之後，家無畜積。

translations.literal: Therefore after he fell into captivity, the household had no stores.
translations.idiomatic: So after he was taken, his household had nothing laid by.

sentences.zh: 及齊受禪，以為都官尚書。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication, he was made director of the masters of punishments.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Qi took the throne, he was made director of the masters of punishments.

sentences.zh: 子秉。

translations.literal: His son Bing.
translations.idiomatic: He had a son, Bing.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：王羆剛峭有餘，弘雅未足。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Wang Pi had stern sharpness in surplus, but magnanimous elegance was not enough.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Wang Pi was more than stern enough, but lacked refined magnanimity.

sentences.zh: 情安儉率，志在公平。

translations.literal: His disposition rested content in thrift and plainness; his will was set on fairness.
translations.idiomatic: He was content with plain living and set his heart on fairness.

sentences.zh: 旣而奮節危城，抗辭勍敵，梁人為之退舍，高氏不敢加兵。

translations.literal: Thereafter he exerted integrity in a perilous city and matched words with fierce enemies; Liang men withdrew on his account, and the Gao clan did not dare bring troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he upheld his integrity in a doomed city and defied fierce foes with bold words, so the Liang forces withdrew before him and the Gao clan did not dare attack.

sentences.zh: 以此見稱，信非虛。

translations.literal: To be famed for this was truly not empty.
translations.idiomatic: His reputation was well deserved.

sentences.zh: 述不隕門風，亦足稱也。

translations.literal: Shu did not let the family tradition fall—also worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Shu upheld the family reputation—also worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 王思政驅馳有事之秋，慷慨功名之際。

translations.literal: Wang Sizheng galloped in the autumn of urgent affairs, at the juncture when one is stirred by fame and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng rode hard in times of urgent crisis, when men are most stirred to win fame.

sentences.zh: 及乎策名霸府，作鎮潁川，設縈帶之險，修守禦之術，以一城之衆，抗傾國之師，率疲乏之兵，當勁勇之卒，猶能亟摧大敵，屢建奇功。

translations.literal: When he had entered service with the overlord's bureau and served as garrison commander at Yingchuan, he established the defenses of an encircling belt and perfected techniques of defense; with the people of one city he resisted a nation-overthrowing army, leading exhausted troops to face fierce and brave soldiers—still he could quickly crush great enemies and repeatedly achieve extraordinary merit.
translations.idiomatic: Once he entered service with Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's bureau and held Yingchuan, he turned its belt of rivers into a fortress and perfected every method of defense. With one city's garrison he faced an army that had mobilized the whole state, leading worn-out troops against fresh and fierce soldiers—yet he repeatedly crushed great enemy forces and won extraordinary victories.

sentences.zh: 忠節冠於本朝，義聲動於鄰聽。

translations.literal: Loyal integrity crowned the court; righteous fame moved neighboring listeners.
translations.idiomatic: His loyalty and integrity were unmatched in the dynasty, and his righteous renown stirred neighboring states.

sentences.zh: 雖運窮事蹙，城陷身囚，壯志高風，亦足奮於百世矣。

translations.literal: Though fate was exhausted and affairs pressed tight, the city fell and he was taken prisoner, his lofty will and noble spirit are enough to stir generations for a hundred ages.
translations.idiomatic: Though fortune failed him, the city fell, and he ended a prisoner, his lofty will and noble spirit are enough to inspire generations for ages to come.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text uses the Zhonghua Shuju, November 1971 edition of the Book of Zhou, as the base for this collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Zhou》 (November 1971).
